properties.name: MEASURED (Grok Build 1.0.30, this box, 2026-09-15): the model receives ONLY the text block of a reflow2 tool result — the session store keeps `rawOutput.output.OkayOutput` = the content text and nothing of structuredContent — so every structured reply is the signpost sentence; Grok Build is a native Rust client on rmcp 3.2.0, names tools `reflow2__<tool>`, and hides all 191 MCP tools behind a SearchTool the model queries first
properties.statement:
Anthony opened Grok Build 1.0.30 on the reflow2 repo itself (2026-09-15 ~02:05Z, served by the 0.59.0 shared daemon via .mcp.json) and ran where-am-i. Its agent reported: "This client only shows the text half of structured replies." Measured from the client's own session store (~/.grok/sessions/<repo>/<session>/): chat_history.jsonl tool_result entries for maturity_report, what_next, scan_nodes and open_questions carry exactly the STRUCTURED_ONLY signpost (857 bytes) as their whole content; updates.jsonl stores each MCP result as {type: MCP, tool_name, server_name, output: {OkayOutput: <content text>}} with NO structuredContent field kept anywhere. So the client discards structuredContent at the transport edge, before storage, and the model never sees it. THE SAME SESSION ALSO PROVES THE DUPLICATE SHAPE WORKS ON THIS CLIENT: get_instructions and get_skill build their result with skills_tools.rs `structured()`, which puts the pretty-printed JSON in the text block AS WELL AS structuredContent, and both reached the model in full (21 KB each, OkayOutput = the JSON). graph_report_markdown (prose only) reached it too. So on Grok Build: signpost → nothing usable; duplicate → the whole answer. What was NOT measured: what Grok Build does with an EMPTY text block plus structuredContent (OpenCode fills the text from structuredContent in that case; Grok's binary is native Rust on rmcp 3.2.0 and cannot be read the way OpenCode's TypeScript could; a headless probe with a mock server was written — scratchpad grokprobe/ — but Grok Build refused it: the free usage limit was reached, so it waits for quota). Three further facts about this client that bear on skills, instructions and the reply budget: (1) MCP tools are named `reflow2__<tool>` (double underscore); (2) Grok Build 1.0.30 does NOT list MCP tools to the model — it exposes a SearchTool ("total_hidden_tools": 191) the model queries by description first, so a tool's description is its only way of being found; (3) it TRUNCATES a tool output at 19.5 KB, spills the full text to <session>/mcp/call-<id>.json and tells the model to query that file with a terminal command — so reflow2's 30,000-char default reply budget is above Grok's own cap, and the last third of a budget-sized reply arrives as a file pointer. Third content-only measurement of the same client population (Alex 2026-08-27 TUI, Alex 2026-08-29 grok-shell 1.0.13, Anthony 2026-09-15 Grok Build 1.0.30) and the second client after OpenCode (2026-09-14). Bearing on the open question: the constraint that killed always-duplicate (157 KB replies) has weakened since reply_budget (2026-09-13) caps every JSON reply at 30,000 chars by default, so duplicating the payload into content costs at most ~2× a bounded reply.

═══ PARTLY SUPERSEDED 2026-09-15, appended, nothing above changed ═══ The CLIENT behaviour measured above is unchanged and this fact stays open for it. The CONSEQUENCE clause — "every structured reply reaches the model as the signpost sentence" — stopped being true for this client at v0.61.1 (#513, chg:the-content-block-is-chosen-per-client): a handshake name starting `grok` now receives the payload duplicated into the text block, the shape this same session measured to reach the model. Still unmeasured, still open: the empty-text-block case, and the 19.5 KB truncation against the 30,000-char budget (the last third of a budget-sized reply still arrives as a file pointer on Grok Build).
